meta.title: Nephrology Literature Update
meta.query: Clinical nephrology — RCTs, systematic reviews & meta-analyses (humans, English)
meta.source: PubMed (NLM) abstracts; summaries and appraisals generated automatically from those abstracts. Each entry links to its PubMed record and DOI.
meta.note: Summaries and PICO are machine analyses of the source abstracts; criteria marked “not specified” were not stated. Read the source before acting clinically.
meta.appraisal_source: Automated critical appraisal (clinical bottom-line, relevance, caveat).

articles.authors: Faravan A, Ghafourifard M, Ghahramanian A, Rahmani A, Areshtanab HN et al.
articles.title: Facilitators of Peer Support Among Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review and Qualitative Meta-Synthesis.
articles.summary: A systematic review and qualitative meta-synthesis of 15 studies identifying facilitators of peer support in CKD. The analysis identified three main themes: cultivating a supportive culture, weaving deep connections/rapport, and engaged/motivated supporters and recipients.
inclusion: Qualitative studies on peer support among patients with chronic kidney disease

appraisal.bottom_line: Successful implementation of peer support programs in CKD depends on the interaction of organizational support, meaningful peer relationships, and active participant engagement.
appraisal.relevance: Helps clinicians and program designers structure effective peer support systems to improve psychosocial outcomes in CKD.
appraisal.caveat: This is a qualitative meta-synthesis of subjective experiences, which cannot establish quantitative clinical efficacy or direct causal links to hard clinical outcomes.

articles.authors: Kafa HS, Hauge SC, Hansen D
articles.title: Bone Anabolic Treatment in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review.
articles.summary: A systematic review of RCTs evaluating anabolic PTH treatment in CKD Stages 4-5D. Only 2 RCTs were included. In a subgroup of CKD Stage 4 (n=5), teriparatide improved BMD at the lumbar spine and femoral neck. In CKD Stage 5D (n=61), teriparatide significantly improved BMD at the total hip compared to control, but adverse events were more frequent.

pico.population: Adult patients with CKD Stages 4-5D, including kidney transplant recipients
pico.intervention: Anabolic parathyroid hormone treatment (teriparatide, natpara, or abaloparatide)
pico.outcome: Change in bone mineral density (BMD) at the lumbar spine, femoral neck, and total hip

inclusion: Randomized controlled trials investigating teriparatide, natpara, or abaloparatide in adult patients with CKD Stages 4-5D, including kidney transplant recipients

appraisal.bottom_line: Teriparatide appears to improve bone mineral density in patients with CKD Stages 4-5D, but the evidence is extremely limited and associated with a higher frequency of adverse events.
appraisal.relevance: Provides insight into potential bone anabolic therapies for advanced CKD patients who are at high risk for fractures.
appraisal.caveat: The review is severely limited by a tiny sample size (only 2 RCTs; one subgroup of n=5 and one trial of n=61), making the safety and efficacy estimates highly imprecise.

articles.authors: Shi X, Fu K, Hu M, Li R, Li H et al.
articles.title: Renoprotective effects and safety of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in diabetic chronic kidney disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 17 RCTs involving 29,192 participants evaluating SGLT2 inhibitors in diabetic CKD. SGLT2 inhibitors significantly reduced HbA1c (MD = -0.40%, 95% CI: -0.44 to -0.36), body weight (MD = -1.36 kg, 95% CI: -1.55 to -1.18), and systolic blood pressure (MD = -2.98 mm Hg, 95% CI: -3.44 to -2.52). No significant differences were observed in eGFR (MD = 0.25 mL/min/1.73 m2, 95% CI: -0.08 to 0.57) or UACR (MD = -31.55 mg/g, 95% CI: -137.21 to 74.12). SGLT2 inhibitors did not significantly increase UTI risk (RR = 1.20, 95% CI: 0.94 to 1.54) but significantly increased volume depletion risk (RR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.16-1.59).

pico.population: Patients with diabetic chronic kidney disease
pico.outcome: Primary renal surrogate markers (eGFR and UACR), secondary metabolic/hemodynamic outcomes, and safety outcomes

inclusion: Randomized controlled trials evaluating SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with diabetic CKD

appraisal.bottom_line: SGLT2 inhibitors in diabetic CKD significantly reduce HbA1c, body weight, and SBP, with neutral short-to-medium term effects on eGFR and UACR, but increase volume depletion risk (RR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.16-1.59).
appraisal.relevance: Reinforces the metabolic and hemodynamic benefits of SGLT2i in diabetic CKD while highlighting the need to monitor for volume depletion.
appraisal.caveat: The neutral short-to-medium term effects on eGFR and UACR contrast with long-term hard outcome trials, likely due to the initial eGFR dip and limited follow-up in some included studies.

articles.authors: Wang X, Liang S, Sun X, Wang F, Tang G et al.
articles.title: Rituximab as Rescue or Add-On Therapy for Relapsing or Refractory Lupus Nephritis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 19 studies involving 445 patients evaluating rituximab as rescue or add-on therapy for relapsing or refractory lupus nephritis. Pooled complete renal response (CRR) rates were 0.33 (95% CI 0.21-0.46), 0.41 (95% CI 0.28-0.54), and 0.42 (95% CI 0.26-0.60) at 6, 12, and 24 months, respectively. Corresponding overall renal response (ORR) rates were 0.67 (95% CI 0.52-0.80), 0.70 (95% CI 0.51-0.86), and 0.66 (95% CI 0.43-0.86). Proteinuria decreased by -2.69 g/day-equivalent (95% CI -3.23 to -2.16), and serum creatinine decreased by -11.79 µmol/L (95% CI -19.86 to -3.72).

pico.population: Patients with relapsing or refractory lupus nephritis
pico.outcome: Complete, partial, and overall renal response rates at 6, 12, and 24 months; changes in proteinuria and serum creatinine

inclusion: Studies of RTX-based therapy in relapsing or refractory LN reporting renal outcomes

appraisal.bottom_line: Rituximab-based rescue or add-on therapy was associated with moderate overall renal response rates (~66-70% across 6-24 months) and reductions in proteinuria and serum creatinine in patients with relapsing or refractory lupus nephritis.
appraisal.relevance: Provides quantitative support for using rituximab in patients with difficult-to-treat, relapsing, or refractory lupus nephritis.
appraisal.caveat: The analysis is limited by the lack of a control group in the pooled estimates (likely reflecting observational or single-arm studies), and the small total sample size (445 patients across 19 studies).

articles.authors: Balasubramaniam G, Almond M, Harnett P, Turner D, Scales J et al.
articles.title: Anakinra versus intramuscular methylprednisolone acetate for gout flares in people with chronic kidney disease (ASGARD): a UK randomised multicentre, double-blind, double-dummy controlled feasibility study with economic, qualitative and safety assessment.
articles.summary: A feasibility RCT comparing subcutaneous anakinra (100 mg daily for 5 days) versus IM methylprednisolone acetate (120 mg) for gout flares in CKD (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2). The trial did not meet its overall feasibility criteria due to under-recruitment, randomizing only 21 participants (mean age 72 years, mean eGFR 44 mL/min/1.73 m2) out of a target of 32. Mean reduction in pain after 7 days was 46.8 from baseline by 100 mm visual analogue score. Anakinra appeared to have a shorter time to pain reduction, but this requires confirmation.

pico.population: People with gout and chronic kidney disease (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2)
pico.intervention: Subcutaneous anakinra 100 mg daily for 5 days
pico.outcome: Feasibility criteria (recruitment, enrolment, crossover/failure, pain assessment completion) and secondary clinical outcomes

inclusion: People with gout and chronic kidney disease (estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 mL/min/1.73 m2)

appraisal.bottom_line: This feasibility trial failed to meet its overall success criteria due to under-recruitment (21 randomized vs 32 planned), though procedural feasibility for data completion and low crossover was demonstrated.
appraisal.relevance: Highlights the challenges of conducting trials for acute gout flares in CKD, a population with limited safe treatment options.
appraisal.caveat: The study was severely underpowered and did not meet its recruitment target, meaning no definitive conclusions about the comparative efficacy or safety of anakinra can be drawn.

articles.authors: Deng J, Liu W, Wang X, Hu J, Zhang H et al.
articles.title: Effectiveness and Safety of Virtual Reality Interventions for Symptom Management in Adults Undergoing Hemodialysis: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 19 RCTs involving 1228 participants evaluating virtual reality (VR) interventions for symptom management in adults undergoing hemodialysis. Compared with usual care or no VR, VR significantly reduced pain during AVF cannulation (MD -2.44, 95% CI -2.91 to -1.97; P<.001), improved gait speed (SMD 0.46, 95% CI 0.11-0.81; P=.01), increased 6-minute walk distance (MD 74.77, 95% CI 40.55-108.99; P<.001), and reduced depressive symptoms (MD -3.48, 95% CI -6.77 to -0.18; P=.04). No serious VR-related adverse events were reported.

pico.comparison: Usual care or no VR intervention
pico.outcome: Symptom-related outcomes (pain, gait speed, 6-minute walk distance, depressive symptoms, anxiety) and safety

inclusion: Randomized controlled trials evaluating VR-based interventions for symptom-related outcomes in adult patients receiving hemodialysis

appraisal.bottom_line: Virtual reality interventions during hemodialysis significantly reduced AVF cannulation pain, improved physical function (gait speed and 6-minute walk distance), and reduced depressive symptoms without serious adverse events.
appraisal.relevance: Offers a novel, non-pharmacological, and safe method to alleviate the high symptom burden (pain, depression, physical deconditioning) in hemodialysis patients.
appraisal.caveat: There was substantial heterogeneity in the pain outcome (I²=66%) and anxiety outcome (I²=61%), and the long-term sustainability and cost-effectiveness of VR in busy dialysis units remain unproven.

articles.authors: Talyshinskii A, Frascheri MF, Tzelves L, Skolarikos A, Geraghty R et al.
articles.title: Changes in renal function in patients with chronic kidney disease after ureteroscopy: a systematic review and meta-analysis from EAU endourology.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 7 studies involving 742 patients evaluating eGFR changes after ureteroscopy (URS) or retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS) in patients with pre-existing CKD. The pooled mean difference in eGFR was +2.8 mL/min/1.73 m2 (95% CI -2.8 to +8.4; p = 0.27), indicating no significant overall change in renal function, with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 89.6%). No study reported progression to dialysis.

pico.population: Patients with pre-existing chronic kidney disease (CKD)
pico.outcome: Postoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and progression to dialysis

inclusion: Studies reporting pre- and postoperative eGFR in patients with established CKD or cohorts including patients with reduced baseline renal function undergoing standard URS or RIRS

appraisal.bottom_line: Ureteroscopy or retrograde intrarenal surgery in patients with pre-existing CKD does not lead to a statistically significant change in overall eGFR (MD +2.8 mL/min/1.73 m2, 95% CI -2.8 to +8.4, p=0.27), and no cases of progression to dialysis were reported.
appraisal.relevance: Reassures clinicians that endoscopic stone management is generally safe for renal function in patients with CKD.
appraisal.caveat: The evidence is of very low certainty, characterized by extreme heterogeneity (I² = 89.6%) and a lack of standardized long-term follow-up across the included observational studies.

articles.authors: Lin K, Li L, Gao J, Zhang Y, Tan H
articles.title: Prevalence and associated factors of chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus in maintenance hemodialysis patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 25 observational studies involving 8,955 participants evaluating the prevalence and associated factors of CKD-associated pruritus (CKD-aP) in maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) patients. The pooled prevalence of any pruritus was 60.0% (95% CI: 57.0-63.0%). Serum phosphorus was positively associated with pruritus in both continuous (OR = 2.03, 95% CI: 1.44-2.87) and dichotomised analyses (OR = 2.93, 95% CI: 1.83-4.69). Diabetes was associated with higher odds of pruritus (OR = 2.64, 95% CI: 1.69-4.14), whereas high-flux hemodialysis showed an inverse association (OR = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.17-0.56).

pico.intervention: Risk factors/associated factors (e.g., serum phosphorus, diabetes, high-flux hemodialysis)
pico.outcome: Prevalence and odds of chronic kidney disease-associated pruritus (CKD-aP)

inclusion: Observational studies reporting prevalence and/or associated factors of pruritus in adult MHD patients, including only multivariable-adjusted odds ratios for associated factors

appraisal.bottom_line: Approximately 60% of maintenance hemodialysis patients experience pruritus, which is consistently associated with higher serum phosphorus (OR = 2.03) and diabetes (OR = 2.64), while high-flux hemodialysis is associated with lower odds (OR = 0.31).
appraisal.relevance: Highlights the massive burden of CKD-aP and reinforces the clinical importance of phosphorus control and dialysis modality optimization in managing this symptom.
appraisal.caveat: As this is a meta-analysis of observational studies, the identified associations are not necessarily causal, and there was substantial heterogeneity and variation in exposure definitions across studies.

articles.authors: Huang M, Wu S, Shen ZH, Zhang SJ, Fu YS et al.
articles.title: Prediction models for sepsis-associated acute kidney injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 15 studies involving 46,490 patients evaluating the predictive performance of risk models for sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI). The pooled C-statistic was 0.817 (95% CI: 0.781-0.847), indicating moderate-to-good discriminative ability, though substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 92.8%). Studies with a low risk of bias yielded superior predictive performance compared to those at high risk (0.847 vs 0.762; P for interaction = 0.010).

pico.population: Patients at risk of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI)

inclusion: Cohort studies focusing on the development and validation of SA-AKI prediction models

appraisal.bottom_line: Existing prediction models for sepsis-associated AKI show moderate-to-good discriminative ability with a pooled C-statistic of 0.817 (95% CI: 0.781-0.847), though performance is highly heterogeneous.
appraisal.relevance: Accurate prediction of SA-AKI could allow for early preventive strategies and closer monitoring in the ICU.
appraisal.caveat: The meta-analysis is limited by high heterogeneity (I² = 92.8%) and a high risk of bias in several included studies; additionally, the external validation subgroup had a very wide confidence interval, indicating high uncertainty.

articles.authors: Cao C, Song H, Shan W, Huang W
articles.title: Pharmacological interventions for vascular calcification in chronic kidney disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 28 RCTs involving 6330 participants evaluating pharmacological interventions for vascular calcification in CKD. Pharmacological interventions did not significantly reduce coronary artery calcification Agatston score, progression, volume, abdominal aortic calcification progression, arterial stiffness, or all-cause mortality. Significant effects were observed for left carotid IMT (MD -0.06 mm, 95% CI: -0.10 to -0.02), common carotid IMT (MD -0.07 mm, 95% CI: -0.14 to -0.00), T50 change (MD 50.25 min, 95% CI: 34.68-65.82), and dp-ucMGP (MD -504.97 pmol/L, 95% CI: -789.72 to -220.22).

pico.comparison: Placebo, standard care, or other controls
pico.outcome: Primary: imaging-defined measures of vascular calcification (Agatston score, progression, volume, abdominal aortic calcification). Secondary: carotid IMT, T50, arterial stiffness, biomarkers, mineral metabolism, and all-cause mortality

inclusion: Randomized controlled trials comparing pharmacological interventions with placebo, standard care, or other controls in patients with chronic kidney disease

appraisal.bottom_line: Pharmacological interventions do not significantly reduce imaging-defined structural vascular calcification or all-cause mortality in CKD, despite improving intermediate biomarkers like T50 (MD 50.25 min) and dp-ucMGP (MD -504.97 pmol/L).
appraisal.relevance: Suggests that targeting early biological pathways (calcification propensity) may not easily translate into reversing or halting established structural vascular calcification.
appraisal.caveat: The review pools highly diverse pharmacological strategies (heterogeneity), and the follow-up duration of the included RCTs may have been too short to detect changes in structural calcification or mortality.

articles.authors: Qing J, Wei W, Wu J
articles.title: Targeted-release Budesonide (Nefecon) versus systemic glucocorticoids for IgA nephropathy: a placebo-anchored indirect treatment comparison of randomized controlled trials.
articles.summary: A placebo-anchored indirect comparison of 3 RCTs evaluating Nefecon (16 mg/day) versus systemic methylprednisolone for IgA nephropathy. Nefecon improved annualized eGFR trajectory by 2.95 mL/min/1.73 m2 per year vs placebo (95% CI, 1.68-4.58), while methylprednisolone improved it by 2.46 (95% CI, 0.94-3.99). The indirect comparison showed no significant difference in eGFR preservation (MD 0.49 mL/min/1.73 m2 per year; 95% CI, -1.62 to 2.59; Pindirect = 0.651). For annualized absolute proteinuria reduction, the indirect comparison favored systemic methylprednisolone (MD 0.43 g/g per year; 95% CI, 0.13-0.73; Pindirect = 0.004). Serious infections were not significantly different (RR 0.55; 95% CI, 0.04-7.16; Pindirect = 0.650).

pico.outcome: Annualized preservation of eGFR, annualized proteinuria reduction, and serious infections

inclusion: Randomized controlled trials evaluating Nefecon (16 mg/day), systemic glucocorticoids, or placebo in adults with IgAN

appraisal.bottom_line: Indirect comparison suggests no significant difference between Nefecon and systemic methylprednisolone in eGFR preservation, though systemic methylprednisolone was associated with greater proteinuria reduction (MD 0.43 g/g per year, p=0.004).
appraisal.relevance: Helps clinicians weigh the trade-offs between localized gut-targeted therapy (Nefecon) and traditional systemic steroids in IgAN.
appraisal.caveat: This is an indirect comparison based on only 3 trials, and the proteinuria and safety findings require cautious interpretation due to differences in measurement methods and follow-up durations.

articles.authors: Li ZL, Li ZY, Pan MM, Liu BC
articles.title: Efficacy and safety of anrikefon in the treatment of diabetic hemodialysis patients with pruritus: a post hoc analysis.
articles.summary: A post hoc analysis of the phase 3 anrikefon-302 study evaluating the selective peripherally restricted kappa-opioid receptor agonist anrikefon (n=67) versus placebo (n=79) in diabetic hemodialysis patients with pruritus. Significantly more patients achieved a >=4-point (29.9% vs 15.2%; p=0.033) and >=3-point (41.8% vs 20.3%; p=0.012) reduction in WI-NRS score at week 12 with anrikefon. The change in WI-NRS score was significantly greater with anrikefon than placebo (-2.86 vs -1.63; p=0.001). Skindex-10 and 5-D itch scores also significantly improved.

pico.outcome: Percentage of patients achieving >=4-point or >=3-point reduction in weekly mean 24h worst itching intensity numerical rating scale (WI-NRS) score at week 12; changes in Skindex-10 and 5-D itch scales; adverse events

inclusion: Diabetic hemodialysis patients with pruritus from the phase 3 anrikefon-302 study

appraisal.bottom_line: In diabetic hemodialysis patients, the kappa-opioid receptor agonist anrikefon significantly reduced pruritus intensity (WI-NRS reduction of -2.86 vs -1.63, p=0.001) and improved itch-related quality of life compared to placebo.
appraisal.relevance: Pruritus is highly prevalent and distressing in diabetic HD patients; anrikefon offers a targeted, effective, and well-tolerated therapeutic option.
appraisal.caveat: This is a post hoc subgroup analysis of a phase 3 trial, which limits its statistical power and increases the risk of type I error compared to a pre-specified primary analysis.

articles.authors: Han M, Sun D, Lu D, Huang X, Kang F et al.
articles.title: Efficacy of Remimazolam for Anesthesia in Patients Undergoing Renal Allograft Transplantation: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.summary: An RCT of 60 patients scheduled for elective living-related renal transplantation randomized to propofol (Group P, n=30) or remimazolam (Group R, n=30) for anesthesia induction and maintenance. Compared with propofol, remimazolam had a longer onset time but provided better hemodynamic stability, more rapid metabolism, negligible injection pain, and no significant impact on hepatic or renal function.

pico.population: Patients scheduled for elective living-related renal transplantation
pico.intervention: Remimazolam for anesthesia induction and maintenance
pico.outcome: Incidence of hypotension during induction, hemodynamic parameters, postoperative recovery, adverse reactions, and pharmacokinetics

inclusion: Patients scheduled for elective living-related renal transplantation

appraisal.bottom_line: Compared to propofol, remimazolam for anesthesia induction and maintenance in renal transplant recipients provides superior hemodynamic stability and less injection pain, despite a longer onset time.
appraisal.relevance: Hemodynamic stability during induction is crucial in renal transplantation to maintain graft perfusion; remimazolam may be a safer anesthetic alternative to propofol.
appraisal.caveat: The study is small (n=60 total) and the abstract does not report the exact quantitative rates of hypotension or statistical significance (p-values) for the primary endpoint.
